big-pickle.source: OpenCode's own free stealth model: pi-ai opencode:big-pickle has reasoning:true with no level map, models.dev provider opencode lists no reasoning options, and there is no vendor documentation to consult. Recording an empty ladder rather than guessing; revisiting needs a live probe against the Zen API with an API key.

claude-haiku-4-5.source: Anthropic Effort docs (docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/effort): the 'Supported models' list for effort is Fable 5/5.1, Mythos 5/5.1/Preview, Opus 4.5-4.8/5/5.5, Sonnet 4.6/5/5.5 and Haiku 5.5 — Haiku 4.5 is not on it, so it has no effort parameter. It still reasons (adaptive budget_tokens), which is why the picker must stay off rather than offer guessed rungs.

claude-opus-4-5.source: Anthropic Effort docs: 'On Claude Opus 4.5, the only extended-thinking-only model that supports effort'; the level table gates max/xhigh per model and leaves low/medium/high for Opus 4.5. models.dev provider opencode independently lists low/medium/high for this id.

claude-sonnet-4-5.source: Anthropic Effort docs: Sonnet 4.5 is absent from the effort 'Supported models' list (Sonnet 4.6/5/5.5 are listed). It reasons with a budget_tokens ceiling, so there is no ladder to expose. models.dev provider opencode also shows only budget_tokens for it.

flint-40b-free.source: models.dev provider opencode — the gateway's own published catalog — lists reasoning_options effort low/medium/high/xhigh/max for flint-40b-free, and the Zen console docs (opencode.ai/docs/zen) serve it on the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint. Recursive's own serving kit (huggingface.co/RecursiveSI/flint, sglang/README.md) states the checkpoint decides on each turn whether to reason and has no switch or budget, so this ladder is the gateway's mapping rather than a vendor reasoning_effort enum.

glm-5.source: Z.AI thinking docs (docs.z.ai/guides/capabilities/thinking): reasoning_effort control is 'only supported by GLM-5.2 and above'; GLM-5 has deep thinking with thinking.type enabled/disabled but no effort parameter.

glm-5.1.source: Z.AI thinking docs: reasoning_effort is 'only supported by GLM-5.2 and above' — GLM-5.1 exposes thinking.type enabled/disabled but no effort parameter.

kimi-k2.5.source: Moonshot Kimi API docs (platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-kimi-k2-thinking-model): reasoning_effort is kimi-k3 only; kimi-k2.5 takes thinking.type enabled/disabled with no effort rungs.

kimi-k2.6.source: Moonshot Kimi API docs: kimi-k2.6 has thinking on by default and can be disabled, but its reasoning_effort column reads 'Not supported' (K3-only).

kimi-k2.7-code.source: Moonshot Kimi API docs: kimi-k2.7-code has thinking always on (thinking.type accepts only "enabled") and reasoning_effort 'Not supported'.

mimo-v2.6-flash-free.source: Xiaomi MiMo Responses API reference (mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/api/chat/responses): reasoning.effort lists none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max/ultra, with minimal mapped to low and xhigh/max/ultra mapped to high. The page also states intensity is not differentiated yet (none disables, every other level enables), but low/medium/high are all accepted values, so they are the rungs this gateway can send. Corrects the empty ladder recorded earlier from reading only the chat-completions and anthropic pages, which document thinking.enabled|disabled and no effort at all.

minimax-m2.5.source: MiniMax API docs (platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-openai-api): reasoning_effort is effective for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash only. MiniMax-M2.x exposes thinking: { type: enabled | adaptive | disabled } — disabled is accepted but ignored, thinking stays on — and no effort ladder. models.dev provider opencode lists no reasoning options for this id.

minimax-m2.7.source: MiniMax API docs (platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-openai-api): reasoning_effort is effective for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash only. MiniMax-M2.x exposes thinking: { type: enabled | adaptive | disabled } — disabled is accepted but ignored, thinking stays on — and no effort ladder. models.dev provider opencode lists no reasoning options for this id.

minimax-m3.source: MiniMax API docs (platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-openai-api): reasoning_effort is effective for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash only. MiniMax-M3 controls thinking with thinking: { type: adaptive | disabled } (on by default) and documents no effort parameter. models.dev provider opencode lists only a toggle for this id.

nemotron-3.5-lightning-free.source: NVIDIA NIM docs for Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (docs.nvidia.com/nim/large-language-models/2.0.10/get-started/advanced/get-started-nemotron-3.5-lightning.html): reasoning is controlled by chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking and thinking_token_budget. No reasoning_effort enum is documented, and models.dev provider opencode lists no reasoning options for this id.

qwen3.5-plus.source: QwenCloud API references: the Anthropic-compatible Messages API (docs.qwencloud.com/api-reference/chat/anthropic) documents output_config.effort only for glm-5.3, glm-5.2, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, qwen3.8-max and qwen3.8-flash, and the OpenAI-chat reasoning_effort table (docs.qwencloud.com/api-reference/chat/openai-chat) names the qwen3.8 family only. qwen3.5-plus thinks through enable_thinking plus thinking_budget, which is also what models.dev provider opencode lists (toggle + budget_tokens).

qwen3.6-plus.source: QwenCloud API references: the Anthropic-compatible Messages API (docs.qwencloud.com/api-reference/chat/anthropic) documents output_config.effort only for glm-5.3, glm-5.2, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, qwen3.8-max and qwen3.8-flash, and the OpenAI-chat reasoning_effort table (docs.qwencloud.com/api-reference/chat/openai-chat) names the qwen3.8 family only. qwen3.6-plus thinks through enable_thinking plus thinking_budget, which is also what models.dev provider opencode lists (toggle + budget_tokens).

qwen3.8-flash.source: models.dev provider opencode — the gateway's own published catalog — lists effort values low/medium/xhigh for this id; pi-ai has no thinkingLevelMap here. Replaces the low/medium/high/xhigh that had been borrowed from Command Code's gateway, which was a guess for a different gateway rather than evidence for this one.

qwen3.8-max.source: QwenCloud OpenAI-chat reference (docs.qwencloud.com/api-reference/chat/openai-chat): qwen3.8-max reasoning_effort options are low, medium and xhigh (default xhigh); high maps to xhigh, so it is not a separate rung. The Anthropic-compatible page (docs.qwencloud.com/api-reference/chat/anthropic) lists the same three for output_config.effort, and models.dev provider opencode agrees. Replaces low/medium/high/xhigh, which offered a rung the vendor does not define.
